children: posted stronger-than-expected Q3 earnings, but its revenue fell short of the Wall Street consensus. With the solid earnings performance, the retail REIT pushed up the lower end of its 2026 adjusted FFO per share guidance range by a penny.
Q3 adjusted FFO per share of $1.15, beating the average analyst estimate of $1.13, rose from $1.14 in Q2 and $1.10 in last year’s Q3.
Q3 revenue of $213.9M, missing the $212.9M consensus, increased from $205.1M in the prior quarter and $183.2M in the year-ago period.
The retail REIT now expects 2026 adjusted FFO per share of $4.58-$4.59, compared with its prior guidance of $4.57-$4.59 and the consensus estimate of $4.53.
executed new leases, extensions, or options on ~ 862,000 square feet of gross leasable area throughout its existing portfolio, compared with 753,000 square feet in Q2.
In Q3, the REIT invested ~$358M in 94 retail lease properties. It started six development or Developer Fund Platform projects for total committed capital of ~$57M.

"During the quarter, we completed a $400M public bond offering at an all-in rate of 5.36%, further strengthening our fortress balance sheet," said President and CEO Joey Agree. "With approximately $2.0B of liquidity, proforma net debt to recurring EBITDA of 3.9 times, and a portfolio that is 99.8% leased, we are exceptionally well-positioned heading into 2027."
stock rose 0.4% in Tuesday after-hours trading.
Conference call on Oct. 21 at 9:00 AM ET.

title: Agree Realty Q3 earnings beat, revenue misses as leasing activity increases
